bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: CTU grid backdown in Rajasthan (13% of run-rate EBITDA exposed; risk up to 6.5% EBITDA if 50% curtailment for full year); DSM regulation uncertainty (sub-judice, impact assessment pending); module cost inflation from ALCM (June 2026); BESS adoption delay; interest rate volatility
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, data-driven, and disciplined; emphasized execution excellence (100% budget adherence), diversification, and client retention; transparent on risks (curtailment, DSM); no financial guidance given but clear capacity targets; tone reflects leadership in C&I renewables
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Run-rate EBITDA (INR1,870cr) is 1.1x reported EBITDA; 99.24% grid uptime indicates near-zero curtailment in STU projects; negative minority interest is accounting artifact of young assets (PAT negative in first 4-5 years); 82% of volume from AA/AAA/MNC clients; 23-year PPA tenor exceeds utility contracts; Apple JV is financial investment, not offtake
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Leverage is framed as "conservative": Debt (net off liquid assets)/Adjusted EBITDA (annualised) of 4.76 for the three months ended Jun 30, 2026 (4.75 FY26, 4.80 FY25, 4.10 FY24), against a stated portfolio target Net Debt to Run-rate EBITDA of 5.0x - 5.5x.
- Balance sheet at Q1 FY27 (INR Million): Gross Block 1,41,381 (FY26: 1,28,232), Net Debt 1,18,092 (FY26: 96,841), Total Equity 58,316 (FY26: 55,235).
- Net debt is allocated by cohort at Q1 FY27 (INR Million): projects operational >1 year 51,549, projects operational <1 year 20,445, under-construction assets 44,838, Unutilised IPO Proceeds -317 and Corporate Loan 1,577.
- "INR 5,237 Mil of IPO proceeds used for debt repayment"; credit rating is CARE AA- Stable.
- FX policy: "Loans in foreign currencies are measured against PPA revenues in respective foreign currencies. Thus, no hedging is required", with the effective interest rate adjusted for interest rate hedging.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Scale leadership: 3.1 GW operational and 5.7 GW total contracted RE power-sales portfolio as India's largest C&I renewable player
- Deep repeat-customer trust: ~74% of FY26 new contracted volumes came from existing clients
- High-quality, long-duration contracted revenue: average PPA tenor of ~23 years across 1,280+ PPAs
- High-credit-quality counterparty base: over 95%/~82% of customers rated A- and above or AA/AAA-rated / MNC subsidiaries
- Early and deepening leadership in the Data Centre/AI demand segment, now ~42% of contracted capacity, up from ~254 MW to 2,380 MW in two years
- Integrated, end-to-end execution platform (development to operations) enabling large annual capacity commissioning (~1.4 GW in FY26)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Input cost, labour and interest-rate volatility — Management explicitly flags fluctuations in raw material prices, labour costs and interest rates among the business and operational risks it is exposed to.
- Foreign exchange exposure — Flagged as a risk in the MD&A; the company also operates cross-border (Dubai, Bahrain, Thailand, Saudi Arabia) with at least one overseas subsidiary reporting in AED, creating currency translation/transaction exposure.
- Supplier and project-execution risk — MD&A explicitly names supplier-related challenges and project execution risks as ongoing exposures for a business that must commission gigawatt-scale capacity annually.
- Regulatory environment risk — Company flags changes in the regulatory environment as a risk factor, relevant given renewable power's dependence on state/central RE policy, grid connectivity and tariff regulation.
- Land-acquisition / execution bottleneck risk — Company identifies land-acquisition as a risk to its construction pipeline, stating it has secured over 90% of the FY27 pipeline in advance specifically to neutralise this risk.
- Customer/segment concentration in Data Centre & AI — ~42% of contracted RE power-sales capacity is concentrated in the Data Centre/AI customer segment, up nearly tenfold in two years, making a large and growing share of the book dependent on a single demand vertical.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: RE Power Sales: 3,100MW operational, 2,600MW contracted; EBITDA margin 83.5% (up from 82%); gross margin stable at 92-93%; RE Services: 555MW operational, 215MW under construction; EBITDA margin 19.6% (up from 14.4%); 74% of new contracts from existing clients
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Self-described as "India's Largest C&I Renewable Energy Provider", serving 593 C&I customers across 1,328 PPAs and contracts as at Jun 30, 2026, with a weighted average PPA tenor of 23.25 years.
- Customer quality is presented as the moat: 81% of clients by MW are "AA/AAA/MNC Subsidiaries" (A 14%, Others 5%) in Q1 FY27, and 95.06% of customers are rated A- and above as at Jun 30, 2026.
- Repeat business is a stated pillar: 79% of new volumes contracted with existing customers (KPI table: share of repeat orders in new contracted volumes 79.09% at Jun 30, 2026, vs 65.73% at Jun 30, 2025).
- Named key customers include Amazon, Google, Meta, Cisco, STT Global Data Center, NTT Data Group, Equinix, Iron Mountain India Data Centers, Princeton Digital Group, L&T Data Center, Ultratech Cements, Grasim Industries, Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals Ltd, Cargill India, Sansera and Saint Gobain.
- Diversification framed as risk reduction: "1,300+ PPAs across 15+ offsite locations and ~1,600 onsite locations across 4 countries", "122 customers across Karnataka and Gujarat STU portfolios alone", and "Presence across 6 states and international markets reduces concentration risk".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Grid backdown risk] "In our 525 MW CTU project in Rajasthan - grid backdowns expected over next 6-12 months due to ongoing transmission system upgradation"; the deck states this represents 13% (INR 239 Cr) of FY27 Run-Rate EBITDA.
- [Recent conversion/listing] The filing is by "Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Limited (Formerly known as Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Private Limited)", listed as NSE - CLEANMAX / BSE - 544717, with ISIN INE647U01026/INE647U08039 and Scrip Code 544717/977267.
- [Rajasthan CTU contracting] "Rajasthan CTU project caters to 3 different Environmental Attribute Purchase Agreements (EAPAs) with global technology companies".
- [Group Captive definition] The glossary defines Group Captive as "Customers Invest Min. 26% Equity, Consume 51% Power as per Electricity Act" versus Third Party Open Access where "Customer Equity Participation Not Required" — a regulatory structure underpinning 48% of operational capacity.
- [FX accounting] On one contract with tariff and debt both in USD, INR depreciation produced an FX gain of INR 157 million in other income and a corresponding FX loss of INR 227 million in other expenses, which the deck says are "broadly offsetting".
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: CleanMax develops, builds, owns and operates renewable energy power projects (wind-solar hybrid, large-scale solar, rooftop/onsite solar, STU & CTU grid-connected plants) and sells the power under long-term PPAs to commercial and industrial customers, complemented by RE services such as energy storage (BESS), asset management and carbon/I-REC solutions. Customers span data centres and AI infrastructure, technology, manufacturing, steel, cement, FMCG, pharmaceuticals, real estate and global capability centres across India and select international markets.

outlook.body: Data & AI demand (42% of contracted capacity, up from 14% in 2024); expansion into new states (Rajasthan, Andhra, Uttarakhand); potential BESS integration (currently 5-7MW); strategic JVs with Apple, Iron Mountain, STT Data; global big tech partnerships (Meta, Google, Amazon)
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Be the long-term net-zero energy partner for corporate India, anchoring growth in long-term PPAs (average tenor ~23 years) with high-quality counterparties rather than one-off sales.
- Deepen leadership in the Data Centre/AI demand segment, which management identifies as the defining infrastructure story of the decade.
- Grow as a disciplined, listed public company focused on assets designed to compound over time, leveraging the IPO for deeper governance and capital to build ahead of demand.
- Expand CTU-connected portfolio and pioneer Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to address evolving regulatory landscapes and capture peak-hour premiums.
- Maintain capital-efficient growth underpinned by disciplined capital allocation and a high-quality, resilient customer portfolio.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 was a record commissioning year, with ~1.4 GW of new RE power-sales capacity commissioned, including the company's first 525 MWp CTU-connected project in Bikaner, Rajasthan. For FY27, management targets a minimum of 1.5 GW of new commissioned capacity (described as a floor, not a ceiling), backed by over 2.6 GW already contracted and under execution. The company is expanding its CTU-connected portfolio, including the 529 MW Koppal hybrid plant, and is pioneering Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to address evolving regulatory landscapes and capture peak-hour premiums. Over 90% of the FY27 construction pipeline has reportedly been secured (land acquisition) in advance to mitigate execution bottlenecks.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- AI, cloud and hyperscale data centres are driving an unprecedented surge in demand for clean, round-the-clock power, positioning CleanMax at the centre of this shift.
- Renewables accounted for the largest share of incremental global energy demand growth in 2025 for the first time, with low-emissions sources meeting nearly 60% of the increase in global energy needs.
- India added a record 55.3 GW of non-fossil capacity in FY26, the highest annual addition in its history, with renewable generation (excluding large hydro) growing 21.1% YoY.
- Policy tailwinds support sector growth: GST on renewable energy devices cut from 12% to 5% (Sept 2025), PLI-driven domestic module manufacturing capacity reaching ~172 GW, and completion of Green Energy Corridor Phase-I facilitating power evacuation.
- The Commercial & Industrial (C&I) segment has become a dominant force in the wind sector, contributing 75% of new wind capacity additions industry-wide.
- Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are emerging as the fastest-growing power technology globally, supported by new tax exemptions in India, positioning storage as a key emerging growth vector.
- 5.7 GW of total contracted RE power sales capacity as of 31 March 2026, comprising 3.1 GW operational and 2.6 GW contracted and under execution.
- 1,280+ Power Purchase Agreements in place across the customer base.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: CleanMax scaled operational capacity to 3.1GW (+1.4GW YoY) with 42% of contracted portfolio now tied to Data & AI, driving 28% EBITDA growth and margin expansion; key risks include CTU curtailment in Rajasthan and upcoming ALCM tariffs, but strong client retention (74%) and diversified STU exposure mitigate downside.
